question: Is Wagyu beef halal if the cows are fed beer?
answer:
My dear brother Ishaq, please do your research, all of you: whenever you ask or want to do anything, do your research, find out what exactly the issue is. And I found this very amusing because it is a common myth.

Firstly, for those of you who do not know, what is Wagyu? Wagyu refers to a particular meat that comes from a particular type of cow that is primarily based in Japan. But obviously, since it has become popular, it has been imported or exported to other places in the world. So it refers to a type of steak that comes from a specific type of cow. And Wagyu is very, very prized. It is perhaps the most expensive steak in the world, or one of the most, because of the unique marbling of the fat and the meat that is intertwined in a way that is not found in other types of cows. And Kobe as well is a type of Wagyu. And so Wagyu is one of the most exotic, if not the most exotic, type of steak.

And there is a rumor (it is a rumor) that one of the reasons why Wagyu is so expensive is because they feed beer to the cows. Now, firstly, I ask you, without even Googling: do you really think they're going to give beer to the cow? Do you really think they're going to make the cows tipsy and just feed them beer? Allahu al-musta'an. No, they're not going to do this. This is a common misconception about Wagyu.

Wagyu is expensive for many reasons, one of them being supply and demand. SubhanAllah, when people want something, the prices are going to go... it's as simple as that. Really, essentially, the Wagyu cow is not any more or less expensive inherently; it's just like anything that people want. Let me give you an example: Ajwa dates in Medina. It costs the exact same amount of money to plant Ajwa as it does to plant all the other dates. It costs the same amount of effort to harvest Ajwa as it does all of the other dates. And yet Ajwa sells for five times the price of regular dates. Why? Because of supply and demand, as simple as that. People want it; khalas, we can overcharge. That's the reality of economics. It's like Adam Smith; this is the reality of economics. Anyway, so Wagyu is expensive not because of the beer.

Now, what if the cows had ingested something haram? I wanted to actually answer this question because it's not just humorous; we can answer it in a more academic manner as well. Our scholars say: a little bit of najasah that is swallowed by the animals is overlooked by unanimous consensus of all the scholars of Islam. Nobody says otherwise. Anybody who says otherwise, frankly, has never been around animals. Do you really expect that a chicken or a cow is going to be eating and no najis is going to come in its food? No. Obviously, if you're a Muslim farmer, it is haram to give najis to the animals. If they eat it on their own without you giving it to them, then a little amount is overlooked.

However, if an amount is given that affects the quality of the meat (I'm just saying theoretically; Wagyu is not of this nature), if an amount of najis product is given that affects the animal, the taste, the smell, the color of the animal, then in this case it is makruh to sacrifice that animal and eat it. And you should leave the animal for a number of days until it becomes pure, so you do not feed the animal anything najis. And this is, again, if you had power over it, if you were the farmer in this case. But otherwise, a little bit of najasah would be overlooked in any case.

So that answers the question: **Wagyu beef is definitely halal.** Of course, in my opinion, it has to be zabihah or kosher as well, so you cannot just buy any.

But I have to conclude this question with a very, very important disclaimer. Beef aside, when it comes to cooking the steak, there is really only one madhhab that is acceptable. All other madhhabs are going to be soundly refuted, and they are batil. There is one madhhab for cooking steaks, and that is medium rare. Please make a note of this. And this is the qawl al-rajih; all the evidences are around this position. Obviously that is a joke, inshallah ta'ala. Or is it? I don't know.
